R1_human_readable.rationale: The PRD clearly explains the agency portfolio, audience, core experience, design language, content, surfaces, and verification criteria in coherent human-readable language.

R2_markdown_formatting.rationale: Headings, nested lists, tables, and inline code are consistently structured and readable in standard Markdown.

R3_no_replica_original.rationale: The PRD neither frames the product as a replica nor catalogs features omitted relative to another site.

R4_no_implementation.rationale: Most visual, behavioral, accessibility, and root-asset requirements are product-facing, but several lines cross into loading strategy, concrete build/config files, DOM structure, identifiers, and HTML rendering internals.

R5_no_submission_artifacts.rationale: The document does not mention Web Craft, validation workflows, required submission deliverables, companion PRD artifacts, or review materials.

R6_scaffold_structure.rationale: All expected scaffold areas are present as predictable top-level sections, with Product Surfaces as the detailed center and a separate, comparatively compact Acceptance Criteria layer.

W1_run_on_structure.rationale: The document is lengthy but scan-friendly; dense inventories and biographies are organized into coherent tables rather than collapsed prose.

W2_screenshot_references.rationale: No screenshots, screenshot directories, or screenshot filenames are referenced.

W3_section_content_placement.rationale: Reusable catalogs and asset mappings are appropriately global, surface-specific behavior remains under Product Surfaces, and Acceptance Criteria summarize rather than reproduce the full specification.

W4_extra_sections.rationale: Every top-level section belongs to the expected scaffold; headings such as Assets and Visuals are subsections within Acceptance Criteria rather than non-standard top-level sections.

summary.overall_rationale: The PRD is coherent, well-formatted, standalone, and follows the expected scaffold without replica framing or warning-level organization issues. It fails only R4 because several requirements document concrete implementation internals, including loading choices, manifest files, DOM identifiers and wrappers, DOM removal, and HTML rendering structure.
